A messenger for people who have sensitive things to say to each other. What is said in Whospair exists only on the two phones, for the time chosen, and nowhere else.

No server. No server relays, stores or sees your exchanges. Each phone is its own access point on the Tor network; messages go directly from one to the other.

No account. No number, no e-mail, no real name. Your identity is a key pair created on this phone. You add each other by scanning a QR code, in person or through a link.

End-to-end encrypted. Messages, voice notes, files and calls are encrypted before they leave the phone, then travel over Tor, which hides your IP address.

Ephemeral. Every message has a chosen lifetime, then disappears on both sides. Nothing is backed up anywhere else.

Live. You can only reach someone who has the app open, or who turned on “Stay reachable”.

Protected on the phone. Everything is encrypted under your PIN. Ten wrong PINs, or the duress PIN, erase everything.

Disclaimer. Whospair is a tool. How you use it is your sole responsibility. It is provided as is, without warranty, and its authors cannot be held liable for its use or its consequences.

Whospair collects nothing. No server receives your data: so there is no one to analyse it or hand it to a third party.

What the app never does: profiling, selling data, advertising, tracking code, crash reports sent anywhere, reading your address book, location. No third-party company receives anything, neither data nor usage signals: the app only talks to the Tor network, to your contacts and to its update distributor.

What stays on this phone, encrypted: your keys, contacts, messages and files — until they expire, you delete them, or after 10 wrong PINs. Photos you send are stripped of their metadata (location, device model).

What others can still see: your network operator can see that this phone uses Tor, but not with whom or what. Your contact sees what you send them, and your profile photo if you allow it.

Updates. Once a day, the app quietly asks, over Tor, whether a newer version exists. This request contains only its version number: no identity, no contacts, no messages.

Why every day? Because an up-to-date version refuses to communicate with a version that is too old. This is deliberate: an old version may contain a flaw. Without updating, you could no longer reach your friends or colleagues; only the update still gets through to you.

Whospair is constantly evolving, hence frequent updates. A flaw can be discovered and exploited before anyone even notices. Fixing quickly keeps your data out of the wrong hands.

Your rights. Since nothing is collected, there is nothing for us to show, correct or delete. Everything is in your hands: uninstalling the app erases it all.

Responsibility. You alone are responsible for what you send, to whom, and what you do with what you receive. Whospair is provided as is, without warranty.
